findings.title: ESET Research: Russian RomCom group exploits new vulnerability, targets companies in Europe and Canada
findings.summary_md: ESET researchers Peter Strycek and colleagues disclosed a previously unknown WinRAR zero-day, CVE-2025-8088, a path traversal vulnerability enabled through NTFS alternate data streams, exploited in the wild by the Russia-aligned RomCom group. ESET telemetry placed spearphishing campaigns between July 18 and July 21, 2025 against financial, manufacturing, defense, and logistics companies in Europe and Canada, delivering SnipBot, RustyClaw, and Mythic backdoors. WinRAR 7.12 was affected; a fixed beta shipped July 24, 2025 and the patched full release followed.

findings.title: WinRAR 7.13 Final released (Critical vulnerability CVE-2025-8088)
findings.summary_md: RARLAB's vendor advisory announces WinRAR 7.13 (release date July 30, 2025), fixing CVE-2025-8088, a directory traversal flaw affecting the Windows versions of WinRAR, RAR/UnRAR, UnRAR.dll, and portable UnRAR that lets crafted archives bypass the user-specified extraction path. Linux/Unix builds and RAR for Android are not affected. RARLAB credits Anton Cherepanov, Peter Kosinar, and Peter Strycek of ESET for the report and calls for immediate action; the news item is dated 12.08.2025 15:00 site time (win.rar GmbH is registered in Germany).

findings.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities: CVE-2025-8088 added
findings.summary_md: CISA added CVE-2025-8088, RARLAB WinRAR Path Traversal Vulnerability (CWE-35), to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 12, 2025, with a required-action due date of September 2, 2025 for federal agencies. The entry carries knownRansomwareCampaignUse: Known and points to the RARLAB advisory and NVD as references.

findings.title: Gamaredon's infection chain: Spoofed emails, GammaDrop and GammaLoad (TRR260501)
findings.summary_md: HarfangLab's report TRR260501 documents a dozen waves of spearphishing against Ukrainian state institutions since September 2025 abusing CVE-2025-8088, with the earliest exploit-bearing email dated September 26, 2025, delivering the GammaDrop and GammaLoad VBScript downloaders through Cloudflare Workers C2 with a kosoyed[.]ru fallback. Spoofed mail was relayed from the 194.58.66.0/24 subnet using stolen credentials, and delivery succeeded largely because impersonated government domains lacked enforced SPF, DKIM, and DMARC. HarfangLab attributes the activity to Gamaredon (UAC-0010) with high confidence and published IoCs and detection rules alongside the report.
